title: Stability as a sum of Fourier weights
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. The noise stability at parameter $\rho$ is the generating sum of the Fourier weights by level: $$\operatorname{Stab}_{\rho}(f)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\rho^k W_k[f],$$ where $W_k[f]=\sum_{S\subseteq[n],\,|S|=k}\widehat f(S)^2$.
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$; for
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i$,
$\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}f(x)\chi_S(x)$,
$W_k(f)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat f(S)^2$ for $k\in\mathbb N$, and
$T_\rho f(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}\rho^{|S|}\widehat f(S)\chi_S(x)$.
The noise stability $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}f(x)T_\rho f(x)$ satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)=\sum_{k=0}^n\rho^kW_k(f).
\]
